mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the sensory and motor routes was most worthwhile: the planned cutaways locate their cell bodies and show how separate axons share a mixed spinal nerve.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the spinal cord produced no available partners, despite its visibly matching central tracts. It clarified the assembly order only indirectly.

surprise.text: The spinal cord could not connect yet; the cerebrum and diencephalon had to be joined before the remaining central structures.

arbitrary.text: The required central assembly order felt somewhat arbitrary: the spinal tracts were anatomically continuous, but no explanation was given for why that connection had to wait.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see the peripheral branches connected to tissues, because this chapter left their endings visibly unconnected. The functional insets were useful, though terms such as diencephalon and medulla received little explanation in the supplied chapter.
